name: Cloudflare Workers
description: Protects against destructive Cloudflare Workers, KV, R2, and D1 operations \ via the Wrangler CLI.

destructive_patterns.name: wrangler-delete
destructive_patterns.description: wrangler delete removes a Worker from Cloudflare.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Cloudflare Worker immediately stops all edge processing for that \ Worker. Any routes pointing to it will return errors. Custom domains and \ bindings (KV, R2, D1) associated with the Worker remain but become orphaned.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - wrangler deployments list: Review deployment history first \ - Disable routes instead of deleting the Worker \ - Use wrangler tail to verify traffic before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: wrangler-deployments-rollback
destructive_patterns.description: wrangler deployments rollback reverts to a previous Worker version.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Rolling back a deployment replaces your current Worker code with a previous \ version. This can reintroduce bugs, break API compatibility, or cause issues \ if the previous version relies on removed bindings or environment variables.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - wrangler deployments list: Review available versions first \ - Test the target version in a staging environment \ - Deploy a fix forward instead of rolling back

destructive_patterns.name: wrangler-kv-key-delete
destructive_patterns.description: wrangler kv key delete removes a key from KV storage.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a KV key immediately removes the data at all edge locations. \ Applications reading this key will receive null or errors. KV deletions \ propagate globally within seconds.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - wrangler kv:key get: Retrieve and backup the value first \ - Set an expiration instead of deleting for temporary data \ - Use KV namespaces for environment separation

destructive_patterns.name: wrangler-kv-namespace-delete
destructive_patterns.description: wrangler kv namespace delete removes an entire KV namespace.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a KV namespace permanently removes ALL keys and values within it. \ Any Workers bound to this namespace will fail when accessing KV. This cannot \ be undone and all data is lost.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - wrangler kv:key list: Inventory all keys first \ - Export data before deletion \ - Remove Worker bindings before deleting the namespace

destructive_patterns.name: wrangler-kv-bulk-delete
destructive_patterns.description: wrangler kv bulk delete removes multiple keys from KV storage.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Bulk delete removes many KV keys at once based on a JSON file. This is \ efficient but dangerous - a malformed keys file can delete unintended data. \ All deletions are immediate and irreversible.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review the keys JSON file carefully before execution \ - Test with a single wrangler kv:key delete first \ - Back up affected keys before bulk deletion

destructive_patterns.name: wrangler-r2-object-delete
destructive_patterns.description: wrangler r2 object delete removes an object from R2 storage.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an R2 object permanently removes the file from storage. Any URLs \ or Workers accessing this object will receive 404 errors. Unlike S3, R2 does \ not charge for delete operations but data is unrecoverable.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - wrangler r2 object get: Download the object first \ - Use object lifecycle rules for automatic expiration \ - Move to a separate 'archive' bucket instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: wrangler-r2-bucket-delete
destructive_patterns.description: wrangler r2 bucket delete removes an entire R2 bucket.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an R2 bucket removes the bucket and ALL objects within it. Workers \ bound to this bucket will fail. The bucket name becomes available for reuse \ by any Cloudflare account.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - wrangler r2 bucket list: Verify the bucket contents \ - Empty the bucket and verify it's truly unused \ - Remove Worker bindings before bucket deletion

destructive_patterns.name: wrangler-d1-delete
destructive_patterns.description: wrangler d1 delete removes a D1 database.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a D1 database permanently removes all tables, data, and schema. \ Workers bound to this database will fail with binding errors. D1 databases \ cannot be recovered after deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - wrangler d1 export: Export the database first \ - wrangler d1 info: Review database details \ - Remove Worker bindings before deletion
